evals.prompt: Deploy the optimized-baseline guide into namespace llm-d-test on my cluster. The llm-d checkout is at ~/src/llm-d.
evals.expected_output: Sets LLMD_PATH, confirms scripts/guide.py exists, summarizes guides/optimized-baseline with list-guide-steps.py, detects the accelerator and maps it to ACCELERATOR_TYPE, checks the llm-d-hf-token Secret and the GAIE CRDs, presents the detected configuration, renders deployments/deploy-YYYYMMDD.sh with guide.py emit (standalone mode, prerequisites.clone excluded), asks for confirmation, executes one section per emit invocation, validates with Kubernetes state only, and asks before running the connectivity test.

evals.prompt: Stand up prefill/decode disaggregation with vLLM on our H200 nodes. We have never installed anything llm-d related on this cluster.
evals.expected_output: Selects guides/pd-disaggregation with ACCELERATOR_TYPE=gpu, MODEL_SERVER=vllm, INFRA_PROVIDER=base (or gke when GKE labels are detected). Detects that the GAIE CRDs and the LeaderWorkerSet controller with DisaggregatedSet support are missing, explains that prerequisites.gaie and prerequisites.lws are cluster-scoped, shows their emitted commands, and runs them only after explicit confirmation. Waits for the DisaggregatedSet roles to become Ready before validation.

evals.prompt: Deploy optimized-baseline but serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with 1 replica instead of the default.
evals.expected_output: Does not edit any file under the llm-d checkout. Creates deployments/<name>/kustomization.yaml with the upstream overlay as base and a patch for the model name and replicas, applies it in place of the emitted deploy.modelserver step, passes the custom MODEL to the router through the emitted variables, and records the customization in deployments/deploy-YYYYMMDD.sh.

evals.prompt: Put llm-d behind our existing GKE Gateway named llm-d-inference-gateway in namespace inference.
evals.expected_output: Selects gateway mode, maps the gke-l7-* GatewayClass to provider.name=gke, emits deploy.gateway instead of deploy.standalone, verifies Gateway PROGRAMMED=True and HTTPRoute ACCEPTED=True, and warns that provider.name=none would produce 503 responses on GKE.

evals.prompt: We have a GKE cluster with TPU7x 2x2x1 nodes. Deploy optimized-baseline there, but serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B instead of the model the guide ships for TPU v7, and keep the EPP off our small CPU node pool.
evals.expected_output: Maps google.com/tpu plus the gke-tpu-accelerator=tpu7x label to ACCELERATOR_TYPE=tpu/v7 with INFRA_PROVIDER=gke, selects deploy.modelserver.standard explicitly (the option(manual) member), and creates deployments/<name>/kustomization.yaml whose resources: entry is a relative path to the upstream tpu/v7 gke overlay. The patch replaces the engine args for the dense model (tensor parallelism over the 8 devices of the host, following the guide's Qwen3-32B TPU reference overlay and docs/infrastructure/providers/gke/tpu/README.md), removes model-specific env entries with $patch: delete, and corrects the llm-d.ai/model label while keeping llm-d.ai/guide. Layers a custom router values file with router.epp.tolerations for the TPU taint and plugin parameters appropriate for the new model instead of the guide's tpu-v7.values.yaml numbers. Records both files in deployments/deploy-YYYYMMDD.sh and never edits the llm-d checkout.
